statements.venue: Letter to National Security Advisor Marco Rubio
statements.quote: We cannot assume that future autonomous or AI-enabled attacks will not target hospitals, electric grids, water systems, or other critical infrastructure. Such an outcome would be unacceptable.

statements.reason: Names autonomous or AI-enabled attacks on hospitals and power and water systems as a serious public safety threat, but does not state mass casualties or loss of control, so it sits between C and B.

record: Sent a letter, alone, asking the National Security Council to hold recurring roundtable discussions with frontier AI developers and security experts on emerging AI threats, including research on interpreting and controlling AI systems, and to brief the Senate Intelligence Committee.
Sen. Young press release and letter, 24 Sep 2026

Introduced, with Sen. Mark Kelly, the Advanced Artificial Intelligence Security Readiness Act, directing the National Security Agency's AI Security Center to write a playbook for protecting US AI systems from foreign theft and sabotage.

Reintroduced, with Sen. Maria Cantwell, the Future of AI Innovation Act, which would write the Commerce Department's Center for AI Standards and Innovation into law to develop voluntary standards and testing environments.
Co-led reintroduction of the CREATE AI Act, which would establish the National AI Research Resource in law.
grade_reason: His 24 September 2026 letter acknowledges serious risks from advanced AI (systems that are hard to predict and control, possible autonomous or AI-enabled attacks on hospitals and power grids) but names neither mass casualties, loss of human control, nor extinction. Nothing found reaches A or B, and nothing dismisses the risk.
notes: Seven web searches ran, none refused. All four statements come from one document, the 24 September 2026 letter, which I read in full as the PDF linked from his press release; quotes were copied from the PDF text with line breaks replaced by spaces. The letter is signed by Young alone, so it is not flagged cosigned_letter. The first quote is a boundary case: a reviewer could argue attacks on hospitals and water systems imply mass casualties (B), but the letter does not say so, and the harm is framed mainly as cyber attack. Left out as level D or too fragmentary: (1) the same letter's sentence that AI agents have 'demonstrated the ability to act in ways their users did not intend' (no consequence stated); (2) his 29 April 2026 press release line about harnessing AI's potential and mitigating its risks (too general); (3) remarks at an Indianapolis Business Journal breakfast, reported 10 March 2025, about AI under China's control enabling surveillance and censorship (China competition, level D); (4) an MLex report of 1 October 2026 (headline: Congress cannot be 'observers' of US AI response) that I could only partly read; it quotes only fragments ('superhuman level of virtue') and paraphrases him as saying a basic regulatory framework is needed, so nothing was quoted from it. Semafor (24 Sep 2026) reported the letter and matches the PDF. Could not open: the February 2025 National Review piece 'Todd Young's AI Playbook' (blocked, HTTP 403); it may contain further remarks on AI risk and is worth a manual check. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act: sources found name only Sen. Sanders as Senate sponsor; no source shows Young co-sponsoring, and I did not check the official congress.gov cosponsor list. His position on the 2025 proposed moratorium on state AI laws was not established and is outside the positions tracked here. Statements before 2025 (for example the 2023 AI Insight Forums he co-hosted) were not included.
